army_commander.name: Major General George Gordon Meade
army_commander.notes: Meade assumed command only 3 days before the battle began.

commander.name: Major General John F. Reynolds
commander.fate: KIA July 1, 1863 — shot through the head at approximately 10:15am while directing the Iron Brigade into Herbst Woods

successor.name: Major General John Newton
successor.assumed_command: July 1, evening — sent by Meade to replace Doubleday

corps.notes: I Corps bore the brunt of July 1 fighting. Nearly 50% casualties — the highest of any Union corps at Gettysburg.

commander.name: Major General Winfield Scott Hancock
commander.fate: Severely wounded July 3 during Pickett's Charge — nail and saddle pommel fragments drove into his thigh

corps.notes: Held Cemetery Ridge on Days 2 and 3. Hancock sent to Cemetery Hill on July 1 by Meade to assess the situation and take command.

commander.name: Major General Daniel Sickles
commander.fate: Right leg amputated July 2 after artillery shell shattered it — Sickles famously smoked a cigar as he was carried from the field

corps.notes: Sickles's unauthorized advance to the Peach Orchard salient on July 2 created the crisis of the second day.
Rushed to Little Round Top on July 2. Vincent's brigade arrived just in time to hold the position.
Largest Union corps. Marched 34 miles in 17 hours to reach the battlefield. Arrived July 2 and served as army reserve — saw almost no direct action.
Routed north of Gettysburg on July 1. Many units were German immigrants — corps unfairly blamed for the collapse that was largely unavoidable given flanking attacks.
Held Culp's Hill. When pulled to reinforce Cemetery Ridge on July 2 evening, Greene's single brigade held the entire hill alone against Johnson's Confederate division.
Buford's division fought the critical dismounted delaying action on July 1 morning. East Cavalry Field action July 3 stopped Stuart from reaching the Union rear.

commander.name: Major General Abner Doubleday
commander.fate: Survived — assumed corps command when Reynolds killed
commander.notes: Doubleday himself commanded the division; when he took corps command Colonel Roy Stone briefly led until division command sorted out.

commander.name: Brigadier General John Gibbon
commander.notes: Gibbon wounded during Pickett's Charge; Harrow assumed division command

commander.name: Major General David Birney
commander.fate: Survived — assumed corps command when Sickles wounded

divisions.notes: Humphreys's division held the Emmitsburg Road line and conducted a fighting withdrawal under heavy pressure.

commander.name: Brigadier General Samuel Crawford
commander.notes: Crawford led the famous charge down Little Round Top's western slope July 2 evening, driving Wofford's Confederates back through the Wheatfield.

commander.name: Major General John Newton
commander.fate: Survived — transferred to command I Corps July 1 evening

commander.name: Brigadier General Francis Barlow
commander.fate: Severely wounded July 1 — left for dead on Barlow's Knoll; Gordon gave him water believing him dying
commander.notes: Barlow and Gordon met after the war — one of the famous post-war reconciliation stories.

commander.name: Major General Carl Schurz
commander.fate: Survived — assumed corps command when Howard went to Cemetery Hill
commander.notes: Schurz was a prominent German-American political figure.

commander.name: Brigadier General Alpheus Williams
commander.fate: Survived — assumed corps command when Slocum went to right wing

divisions.notes: Geary's division held the right of Culp's Hill. Greene's brigade (U-XII-2-3) held the entire hill alone on the night of July 2.

commander.name: Brigadier General John Buford
commander.fate: Survived Gettysburg — died of typhoid fever December 1863

divisions.notes: Buford's dismounted cavalry delaying action on McPherson's Ridge July 1 morning bought time for Reynolds to bring up I Corps.
Gregg and Custer blocked Stuart at East Cavalry Field on July 3.

commander.name: Brigadier General Judson Kilpatrick
commander.notes: Kilpatrick ordered Farnsworth's suicidal charge July 3. Farnsworth was killed.
